note: **THE SECOND INSTRUMENT AT-03.15 NAMED, BUILT.** AT-03.15 drives `Facade` methods; its own note records that **31 of the 32 verbs it could not reach appear nowhere in the facade surface**, so no number of extra cases there could ever reach them. This is the CLI-level driver: it runs the real binary via `CARGO_BIN_EXE_intent` over a fixture built BY the binary (`init` + six `st new`, never hand-written), snapshots the projected estate `(path -> bytes, mtime)` around each verb, and asserts `{p : mtime differs} == {p : bytes differ}` as SETS. **THE OBSERVABLE IS NAMED, WHICH AT-03.15 REQUIRED OF THIS FILE:** every file under the project root EXCLUDING `intent/.cache/`. Same definition as AT-03.15 and for the same reason -- the store is the durable SSOT, not a projected artefact, so counting the DB's own writes as estate churn would red every verb that reads. **The two obvious alternatives are both wrong and vc measured why:** `did any file appear` trips on pure reads (`st list --status all`, classified `read`, materialises the store from a clean start -- reproduced here), and `the tracked tree` is blind to that same write because `.cache` is gitignored (D29). **The store is therefore OBSERVED SEPARATELY per case rather than dropped**, and it has a paired control in the same run: `todo list` and `ingest` are driven from the identical storeless start and only `todo list` materialises one, so the observation is not stuck-false. **EVERY CASE DECLARES AN EXIT CODE, AND THAT IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF.** A verb that does not run writes nothing, and *wrote nothing* is what passing looks like -- so a snapshot-only driver goes green against a refusing binary, a typo'd subcommand, or a fixture the verb cannot act on. **This is ic's rule in its general form: a run that did not measure must read UNMEASURED, never green.** ic stated it about `cargo test --no-fail-fast` returning 101 for a build failure and a test failure alike; the same hole at a CLI driver is an rc nobody checked. **IT FIRED ON ITS OWN FIRST RUN, UNPLANTED:** the `todo done` case was declared a writer, exited 1 on `st.done is not a legal transition for ST0002, which is triage`, and left the estate untouched -- both guards caught what a set comparison would have reported as a clean pass. The fix was a fixture prep, not a relaxed assertion. **A second unearned claim in this file was caught the same way and by the same discipline:** the `todo list` case's stated reason asserted store materialisation while its prep never removed the store, so the reason was true and the case did not drive it. The prep now does. **WHAT DRIVING THE TEN ACTUALLY FOUND, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THE DEBT LIST IMPLIED: ONLY THREE OF THEM WRITE.** `st sync --write` (real, and the mutate is behind the flag -- the bare form is a dry run, so a driver running it proves nothing, which is the `at lint --fix` trap over again); `todo done` (real, on an acceptance-exempt thread); and `todo update`, which was never on the list and is the todo family's ACTUAL mutator. **The other seven are classified `mutate` on a surface that never drove them:** `st bootstrap` and `st repair` exit 2 with *is a known command that is not implemented yet*; `at lint --fix` exits 1 with *not implemented in v3*, so the flag that earns `at lint` its classification does not exist; `todo` and `todo list` exit 0 and, driven with `intent/todo.md` ABSENT, **print the view and do not create it** -- which is the exact write their own `--help` promises (*generates it if absent*); `ingest` reads and creates no store; and **`todo notdone` and `todo toggle` refuse in EVERY state driven -- a triage thread, a wip thread, a not-started WP, and a genuinely Completed thread** -- because a reopen must record a reason and neither verb can carry one, so they route to `st reopen` and are unreachable including in the one state they nominally serve. **THAT IS A POPULATION DEFECT IN THE DISPATCH TABLE, REPORTED RATHER THAN QUIETLY RE-BUCKETED: six shipped `mutate` entries write nothing at all, two of them documented as performing a write that does not happen.** It is the AC-03.14 class arriving from the other direction -- the criterion exists for *a verb writing a file nobody had written down*, and this is *a file written down that no verb writes.* **Membership is DRIVEN, never asserted:** each of the seven is run against the real binary and required to produce both its exit code AND an unchanged estate, so the day one starts writing this file goes RED and forces the re-bucket instead of leaving an excuse behind. **MUTATION-PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AT THE SUBJECT RATHER THAN THE HARNESS** (cc 2026-08-21). The fix this criterion demanded is one skip at one writer (`write_set.rs`, *a path whose bytes already match is not written at all*). Removing it -- `let unchanged = ...` -> `let unchanged = false`, one token -- reds this file (`st sync` moved 20 changed 1; `todo done` moved 15 changed 4) AND reds 13 verbs in AT-03.15 (`sync --to-disk` 17 moved, 0 changed), while **every write-nothing case stays clean in the same run**, which is the paired control: the mutation reds exactly the writers. Restored from a byte copy in the same tool call, sha256 verified identical. **The estate carries six threads rather than one deliberately**, because on a one-thread fixture *rewrote everything* and *wrote what changed* are the same set, and the assertion would hold against the very defect it exists to catch. **AND THE VERB SET IS ENUMERATED AND PRINTED**, which the criterion requires in as many words, so a verb added to the surface and not driven here is visible rather than silently absent.
